items.title: Major players Lenskart, Groww, Adani Energy join MSCI India Index
items.description: MSCI announced changes to India indices, adding four stocks and removing three.  India's weight in the MSCI India Standard Index will rise slightly to 11.9 percent.  Lenskart Solutions and Adani Energy Solutions are among the new inclusions.  Astral and Balkrishna Industries will move to the Smallcap Index after exclusion.  These changes will take effect on August 31, impacting fund flows.

items.title: Top FPIs ride out storm, outrun Nifty & Sensex in Q1
items.description: During the June quarter, leading international funds encountered remarkable gains within Indian equities, significantly boosting their reported portfolio values. This strong performance exceeded that of key Indian stock market indices, primarily driven by astute investments in mid- and small-cap companies, reinforcing India's reputation as a promising landscape for discerning stock pickers.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced a slight decline on Thursday, influenced by elevated crude oil prices. Investors remained cautious due to positioning ahead of the weekly Sensex expiry, despite a supportive global outlook. The Nifty50 and Sensex both closed marginally lower, reflecting a market lacking strong directional triggers. Elevated crude prices and geopolitical uncertainty kept domestic investors hesitant, suggesting a range-bound market.

items.title: For Friday | Stocks in news: Indigo Paints, LG Electronics India, Tata Motors PV, Honasa Consumer, Ashok Leyland and Physicswallah in focus
items.description: Indian equity markets saw a decline on Thursday, August 13, with the Nifty 50 closing lower. Persistent Middle East tensions and a stronger US dollar influenced investor sentiment negatively. Several companies like Indigo Paints and LG Electronics India reported their first-quarter earnings results. Other firms such as Ashok Leyland and Physicswallah will release their results on Friday. Corporate developments and earnings will guide trading in upcoming sessions.

items.title: Bank of America's $1.9 billion Jio bet shows global banks want a slice of India's retail lending market
items.description: Bank of America is set to invest a substantial $1.9 billion into Jio Financial's Jio Credit, marking a significant show of confidence in India's booming retail loan sector. This collaboration merges Jio's innovative digital capabilities with the seasoned financial knowledge of Bank of America, enabling a strategic expansion in the rapidly growing Indian economy. Regulatory approvals will be required to finalize this impactful venture.

items.title: Corporate cover rates decline amid ample capacity
items.description: Insurance rates for fire, cyber, professional indemnity and directors’ liability fell sharply in the June quarter as abundant capacity intensified competition. Marsh India expects the buyer-friendly market to persist, with companies using lower prices to secure broader coverage and higher limits.

items.title: Karnataka HC quashes ED money laundering case against Sammaan Capital
items.description: The Karnataka High Court has quashed ED money-laundering proceedings against Sammaan Capital, formerly Indiabulls Housing Finance, ruling that the case could not continue after its underlying predicate offences ceased to sustain the allegations.

items.title: LEAP India shares to list today. Check GMP ahead of debut
items.description: LEAP India IPO:  The public issue, which was open for subscription between August 7 and August 11, was subscribed 8.38 times overall. The retail investor portion was booked 1.71 times, while the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) category saw 16.84 times subscription and the non-institutional investor (NII) segment was subscribed 12.64 times.

items.title: Technocraft Ventures shares to list today. GMP signals 17% listing gains ahead of debut
items.description: The healthy GMP comes after an impressive subscription response. The IPO, which was open from August 7 to August 11, was subscribed 38.69 times overall, reflecting robust investor appetite across investor categories.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: BLS International, NBCC India among 5 stocks that could give 10-60% return
items.description: Brokerages remain positive on a host of stocks, with Nuvama Securities initiating a bullish stance on BLS International, while Elara Securities favours Gujarat Fluorochemicals and NBCC India.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.title: Bonus issue alert! Last day to buy this multibagger smallcap clothing stock for 5:1 bonus reward. Do you own?
items.description: Only those shareholders who hold Bizotic Commercial shares in their demat accounts as of Monday will be eligible to receive the bonus shares. As per Sebi's T+1 settlement cycle, investors must buy the company's shares at least one trading day before the record date for them to be credited to their demat accounts and qualify for the bonus issue. This makes today the last day to buy the stock to be eligible for the bonus shares.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 10 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 10 stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 13, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. Traders use the 200-day daily moving average (DMA) as a key indicator to determine a stock's overall trend. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: These large- and mid-cap stocks can give more than 25% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Looking at what happens in the short term is important, as it does have an impact on stock prices. But also always keep an eye on the macro picture. Consider, for instance, this important change: FIIs are no longer the only large source of equity flows. DII money has become much more significant over the years. That does not make the market immune to foreign selling; but it does mean that sustained selling by FIIs need not produce the kind of market reaction it once did.

items.title: Galaxy Surfactants shares hit 20% upper circuit as Q1 profit more than doubles YoY to Rs 166 crore
items.description: Galaxy Surfactants shares hit a 20% upper circuit after the company reported a 109% year-on-year jump in Q1FY27 net profit to Rs 165.9 crore. Revenue rose 38.5%, while EBITDA surged 87% to a record Rs 252.5 crore, supported by stronger volumes, product mix and speciality care demand.

items.title: Jubilant Foodworks shares rally 6% after Q1 results; Bernstein sees Popeyes as strong growth driver. Should you buy?
items.description: Jubilant FoodWorks shares rose to Rs 521 after Q1 FY27 revenue increased 14% year-on-year to Rs 2,570 crore, while EBITDA grew 10% to Rs 360 crore. Domino’s India posted 2.5% LFL growth, while Popeyes delivered 97% revenue growth. Bernstein and Motilal Oswal retained positive ratings, citing Popeyes momentum and prospects for improved margins and growth.

items.title: Brokerages initiate coverage on Vedanta Aluminium, Kalyan Jewellers, 3 other stocks with up to 36% upside
items.description: A host of domestic and global brokerages have initiated coverage on select Indian stocks across sectors such as banks and consumer discretionary. Analysts are bullish on major names such as Kalyan Jewellers among others and forecast strong upside from current market levels. Here is a list of 5 stocks on which brokerages initiated coverage.

items.title: Welspun Living shares rally 11% after Q1 profit jumps 85% YoY. Should you buy, sell, or hold?
items.description: In a notable rise, Welspun Living shares gained traction following the announcement of solid Q1FY27 earnings, showcasing an eighty-five percent increase in profit year-on-year and a twenty-four percent boost in revenue. Financial experts, including those from Motilal Oswal and JM Financial, have reiterated buy recommendations, forecasting ongoing revenue and margin improvements. Significant contributions are expected from the home textiles division and the emerging US pillow segment.

items.title: Honasa Consumer shares jump 4% after record Q1; Jefferies, Emkay forecast strong upside
items.description: Honasa Consumer’s shares rose after Q1FY27 PAT surged 116.5% YoY to a record ₹90 crore, while revenue grew 27% to ₹756 crore and EBITDA jumped 141% to ₹110 crore.

items.title: LG Electronics shares jump 5% after robust Q1 earnings. What are Jefferies, other brokerages saying?
items.description: In the first quarter of FY27, LG Electronics India showcased impressive profit growth alongside significant operational revenue increases from April to June. The surge stemmed from robust demand for premium products across various categories. Analysts remain optimistic, highlighting the company's solid earnings potential and market stance, bolstered by strategic investments focused on enhancing manufacturing and export capacities.

items.title: Tata Motors PV shares fall 5% after weak Q1 results. What are Morgan Stanley, Nomura, others saying?
items.description: Tata Motors’ Q1 FY27 net profit plunged 80% YoY to ₹775 crore due to supply disruptions, Middle East tensions and Jaguar’s wind-down, while revenue rose 9% to ₹95,799 crore and EBITDA margin narrowed to 7.4%.

items.title: Sensex falls 300 points, Nifty below 24,350. Here’s why analysts see range-bound trade
items.description: Indian stock markets opened lower on Friday, with Sensex falling over 300 points and Nifty declining 68 points, remaining range bound despite stable oil prices near $87 a barrel. Metal and auto stocks led losses, while broader markets stayed muted. Market breadth remained positive, with advances outnumbering declines on NSE.

items.title: Astral among 5 stocks flashing bullish signals, indicating possible uptrend
items.description: On August 13, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 4% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns to assess the potential continuation of upward price momentum.

items.title: Sarda Energy among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 13, four Nifty500 stocks rallied over 4% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from stockedge.com. It is an uptrend signal if the RSI value has crossed above 50 from below, indicating that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, which suggests strengthening momentum in the price of the stock. This can indicate potential upward movement and may be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: India won political freedom in 1947. Financial freedom is the next frontier
items.description: Navneet Munot, MD and CEO of HDFC AMC, writes on how Indian households are building financial freedom through capital markets, UPI, and systematic investment plans. With mutual fund assets crossing Rs 82 lakh crore and strong domestic flows, Indian investors are steadily securing their future, one SIP at a time.

items.title: FIIs dumped nearly Rs 1 lakh crore worth of these 10 stocks but 8 defied the selloff
items.description: Foreign investors sold nearly Rs 1 lakh crore from ten Indian stocks. Eight of these companies saw their stock prices increase despite the selling. Bajaj Finance led the gains with a twenty-five percent jump during the quarter. Strong earnings results helped most stocks defy the foreign selloff. FIIs turned net buyers in July after months of significant outflows.

items.title: Technocraft Ventures shares make strong debut, list at 34% premium
items.description: Technocraft Ventures made a remarkable debut on Dalal Street, soaring by 34% on its first day. The IPO drew significant interest, particularly from Non-Institutional Investors. The funds raised will be directed towards enhancing working capital, facilitating business growth, and boosting operational efficiency. Notably, Technocraft Ventures has also demonstrated impressive financial performance with increased profits in the last fiscal year.

items.title: Manorama Industries shares surge over 8% after strong Q1 results
items.description: Manorama Industries shares surged after Q1FY27 net profit jumped 67.6% YoY to ₹78.7 crore, aided by a better product mix, higher capacity and strong demand from chocolate, confectionery and cosmetics sectors.

items.title: Rakesh Jhunjhunwala death anniversary: 5 market lessons every investor should learn from the Big Bull
items.description: On Rakesh Jhunjhunwala’s fourth death anniversary, his investment philosophy continues to offer valuable lessons for investors. From patience and discipline to respecting market dynamics, learning from mistakes and avoiding unreasonable valuations, these principles remain relevant for navigating equity markets.

items.title: Explained: Why Balrampur Chini, Dhampur Sugar, Dalmia Bharat & other sugar stocks are up 12% in 2 days
items.description: Sugar stocks rallied for a second session on Friday as domestic sugar prices climbed 8-10% over the past month to a seven-year high. Rising global prices, supply concerns in Brazil and Thailand, higher ethanol demand and expectations of tighter Indian exports have strengthened the outlook for sugar producers.

items.title: Praj Industries shares rally 7% after Q1 profit more than doubles YoY
items.description: Praj Industries shares surged 6.5% after Q1FY27 net profit more than doubled year-on-year to Rs 12 crore, while revenue rose 12% to Rs 716 crore. The company reported Rs 1,000 crore in order intake and ended the quarter with an order backlog of Rs 4,589 crore, providing strong execution visibility.

items.title: Jefferies’ Chris Wood spots a hidden risk in Big Tech’s $165 billion AI capex race
items.description: Big Tech’s AI capex surge is putting pressure on free cash flow, with Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta spending $165 billion in Q2 against just $7 billion in free cash flow. Jefferies’ Chris Wood warns that growing reliance on cash-burning AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic could pose a hidden risk.

items.title: Sammaan Capital shares fall 4% after Q1 profit declines 27% YoY to Rs 243 crore, revenue drops 31%
items.description: Sammaan Capital reported a 27% YoY decline in consolidated profit to Rs 243 crore in Q1FY27, while revenue from operations also fell. The company reported Rs 56,239 crore in AUM and Rs 3,875 crore in disbursements, with plans to accelerate growth and reduce funding costs.

items.title: Explained: Why Vedanta Aluminium, Hindalco, Nalco shares tumbled up to 7% on Friday
items.description: Vedanta Aluminium, Hindalco and NALCO fell as aluminium prices retreated after Norsk Hydro resumed Alunorte refinery production, easing supply shortage concerns.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Goldman Sachs maintains buy Solar Industries; Morgan Stanley retains Equal Weight on Tata Motors
items.description: Brokerages remain constructive on Solar Industries and Jubilant FoodWorks on strong growth prospects, while Morgan Stanley stays cautious on Tata Motors amid JLR margin and execution risks.
